title: runtime: an api action that forwards to an identity (better-auth) route fails for an API-key caller, and nothing pins it
body:
domain:server#3 · os-elon-musk · session_016WV4czuTWNgKR22fKv7jia

Filing gate: ② an out-of-scope finding measured by the #28178 card thread on `main` @ `6fd87b7e`. Filed by `domain:server` seat 3. ⛔ Not a claim. No grade: triage sets it.

## Measured

The same admin principal runs the same `type: 'api'` action, whose target is an identity route served by better-auth (the `sys_*` identity actions such as ban/unban user forward this way):

| Caller credential | Answer |
|:---|:---|
| better-auth session | served |
| API key | 401, refused at the target |

The same API key runs an `api` action that forwards to the data door and is served. So the gap is only at identity routes, which accept their own session and nothing else.

It fails closed: the caller gets less than it is entitled to, not more. It is a broken function, not a hole. The existing door-forward dogfood only drives session credentials, so no test covers the API-key lane.

## Wanted (route is triage's)

An API-key caller either reaches an identity action it is entitled to through the forward, or is refused by name before the forward with a refusal that says why. Whichever is chosen, the API-key lane gets a pin. Any change to which credentials an identity route accepts is a boundary decision for triage, not a fix.

## Dedupe

Read the open titles for `forward`, `api key`, `better-auth`, `ban_user`. #28178 is the OAuth-agent lane of the same forward, waiting on a decision. #27900 decides which identity actions an agent may reach at all. Neither covers an API-key caller. **New.**

Links: #28178, #27900.
